title: Lexeme resolution attribution and prefetch crediting
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add end-to-end instrumentation that attributes per-lexeme (subtoken) latency and cost to request traces, with a model for amortizing prefetch/prefill KV cache work across subsequent tokens. Deliverables: OTLP span and metric schema, Prometheus metric names + exemplars, a LogQL/Elasticsearch mapping for token events, a lightweight crediting algorithm for prefetch work that updates cost dashboards, and rollout plan with sampling and fallback for high-throughput paths.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP span produced for each generated lexeme with fields: request_id, seq_index, lexeme_text (hashed), lexeme_ms, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hit=true|false, batch_id, model_variant
Prometheus metrics exported: redwood_lexeme_latency_ms_bucket (labels: model_variant, kernel), redwood_kv_prefetch_credit_total, redwood_lexeme_count{kv_hit=true|false}
Grafana dashboard panel that breaks request-level token latency into kernel / kv / queue components and shows per-request amortized prefetch credit
Console can show top-20 requests by lexeme cost and reconcile to billing reports within 5% on a sampled workload
Sampling rate can be dynamically lowered when pod CPU > 75% without dropping span context or breaking aggregates
End-to-end integration tests (unit + e2e) demonstrating a KV prefetch that covers 3 subsequent tokens and how the credit is amortized in metrics
implementation_notes: Instrument at tokenizer output boundary so lexeme text is hash-only in telemetry (PII-safe). Use deterministic murmur3 hash truncated to 64 bits.
Span design: parent span is request; create child spans per lexeme with attributes 'redwood.lexeme.index', 'redwood.lexeme.ms', 'redwood.kv.hit', 'redwood.kernel.ms', 'redwood.batch.size'.
Export a Prometheus exemplar by wiring OTLP -> metrics translation (use p99 exemplar link to trace id for expensive lexemes).

Prefetch credit model: when a prefetch request is issued, record prefetch_cost_ms; allocate credit to following N lexemes where N = min(remaining_cache_ttl_tokens, 8). Credit amortized proportionally to lexeme.kernel_ms. Track leftover credit as redwood_kv_prefetch_credit_unallocated.
Sampling: default 1% of requests, with adaptive bump to 5% for requests that exceed 300ms tail latency; sampling decisions must keep trace id stable across retry/fallback.
Backpressure: if the span emission path fails, fallback to aggregated counters per-request (sum latency, kv_hits) to avoid affecting runtime.
Storage: token events should be routed to a low-cost partition (hot for 7 days, cold for 30) and only persist hashed lexeme text and labels.
grafana_queries:
# request-level lexeme breakdown: sum of lexeme spans grouped by request_id
sum by (request_id) (increase(redwood_lexeme_latency_ms_sum[5m]))

# amortized prefetch credit per request
sum by (request_id) (increase(redwood_kv_prefetch_credit_total[5m])) / sum by (request_id) (increase(redwood_lexeme_latency_ms_count[5m]))

# top lexemes by exemplar trace
topk(20, rate(redwood_lexeme_latency_ms_sum[1m]))
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'lexeme_attribution_v1' on runtime and telemetry-service.
2) Start with 1% sampled traffic for read-only exporting. Verify no P95 CPU increase across pods (target < +3%).
3) Enable prefetch-credit bookkeeping in metrics for 0.1% of traffic and compare totals to offline simulation for 48h.
4) Gradually increase sampling to 5% then 20% while monitoring cost and overhead, then enable for full traffic if stable.
5) Post-rollout: 2-week run with dashboards enabled and automated alert if credit allocation variance > 10% vs simulated baseline.
testing_plan: Unit tests for span attribute generation (including hash invariants).
Integration test that simulates: cache miss -> prefetch -> 3 lexemes hit the prefetched entries and validate credit allocation metrics.
Load test with 30,000 rps sampling to ensure exporter backpressure path maintains <2% additional latency.
E2E reconciliation test comparing sampled telemetry to billing ledger on synthetic workload (target <5% discrepancy).
safety_and_privacy_notes: Never log raw lexeme/plaintext; store only hashed lexeme fingerprints and token-length buckets.
Telemetry must strip user-provided tool output and function returns prior to hashing when flagged by prompt markers.
Add KMS-encrypted environment for any retention of hashed-text index used for debugging.
